Contributing to RdistNN

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Read AGENTS.md before editing. The design index routes interface, validation and numerical contracts; the package scope distinguishes supported and experimental workflows. Open an issue before proposing a new estimator or exported-interface change.

Development and production workflow

Work on local development and keep it unpublished until publication is authorized. Branches in a public GitHub repository are public when pushed. For an authorized production update, publish a review branch, open a PR to master, complete review and required checks, then squash-merge. Direct pushes to master require an explicit override. Keep development current with the reviewed production state.

The first development commit after production 0.1.x establishes 0.1.x.9000. Each subsequent development commit increments the fourth component, including small changes: 0.1.x.9001, 0.1.x.9002, and so on. Uncommitted drafts do not advance this sequence. Read the current version from DESCRIPTION and the current NEWS.md heading; update both together. By default, each production merge becomes 0.1.(x+1); the maintainer may choose another version. After that release, append .9000 to the selected production version to start development. For example, the cycle after production 0.1.2 starts at 0.1.2.9000, then 0.1.2.9001; its next default production version is 0.1.3.

Current development compatibility

Use the current documented interfaces and complete current fit schemas. During this early development stage, remove compatibility layers for older package versions: retired aliases and wrappers, saved-state upgraders and migration shims. Keep one current implementation unless the maintainer explicitly requests an exception. Older, incomplete or inconsistent fits require an actionable refit error; do not silently reconstruct or repair them. Current fits must still survive serialization and support documented reuse.

Document intentional interface changes and update their regression tests. Preserve historical changelogs, released tags/assets and frozen scientific evidence. Compatibility and deprecation commitments can be revisited when the packages stabilize; prior production releases do not change the current policy.

See the lifecycle policy for the package lifecycle and release context.

Local setup

Use R 4.1.0 or newer and a C++17 toolchain; OpenMP is optional. From the root:

install.packages(c("devtools", "pkgdown", "rcmdcheck", "yaml"))
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

Use roxygen2 8.0.0, as declared in DESCRIPTION, to avoid generated-file drift. Install the declared version if needed:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_version("roxygen2", version = "8.0.0", upgrade = "never")

Editing and checking

Changed surface Edit and verify
Function help or exports Edit roxygen in R/; run devtools::document(). Never hand-edit NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd or RcppExports.*.
README Edit README.Rmd; run devtools::build_readme().
Examples or articles Use small seeded examples, guard optional packages, execute changed code and check links/generated output. Refer to the paper for theory.
Behavior or validation Add focused testthat regressions. Select suites using the test map; use the full suite for shared or broad changes.
Release candidate Run the full package/site and cross-platform gates in RELEASING.md.

Preserve public inputs, defaults and result schemas during editorial changes. Identify oracle quantities and distinguish demonstrations from manuscript evidence. Update NEWS.md for user-visible changes.

Run the alignment checks relevant to the changed surface:

Rscript tools/ci/check_tests_declared_deps.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_repository_hygiene.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_pkgdown_reference_coverage.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_generated_file_drift.R
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/ci -v

The generated-file gate regenerates namespace, Rd topics and Rcpp glue in an isolated tree using the declared roxygen2 version. Hygiene checks staged/new candidate files and duplicate top-level R function ownership; local closures may reuse names. Keep check output, archives and private session records under ignored archives/, excluded from source packages. Reuse successful checks while the verified content is unchanged. Reserve build/ for R-generated package metadata, including the vignette index.

Developer analysis tools

These optional checkout tools do not change package installation requirements. On Ubuntu/WSL, the native profiles use Clang 18 (clang++-18, clang-tidy-18, llvm-symbolizer-18), LLVM OpenMP, Bear, ccache and Make. They also need Rcpp and testthat in the selected R installation. Run from this repository root:

python3 tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py doctor
python3 tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py build
python3 tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py compdb
python3 tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py tidy
python3 tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py sanitize --sanitizer-smoke

build installs a fresh private source copy and runs focused installed native and portable-parity tests. compdb repeats that build with caching disabled under Bear, then retains the source and compile_commands.json for tidy. Run compdb again after native inputs, tooling, compiler or R changes; an ordinary build invalidates the previous database. Analysis covers handwritten translation units and headers; generated Rcpp glue still enters the build and database. Use --jobs 1 to reduce compiler concurrency; the maximum is two.

tidy also verifies the retained native/configuration bytes and database against their successful capture. A changed retained copy, edited database or incomplete receipt requires a fresh compdb; analysis never silently repairs that proof.

The default clang profile uses LLVM OpenMP; --profile clang-serial explicitly disables it and --profile gcc selects the normal GCC comparison. Sanitizers require a Clang profile. These Linux profiles complement the release matrix.

Logs, private installations, source hashes and command provenance stay under archives/cpp-tooling/PROFILE/. The project cache lives under archives/cpp-tooling/cache/, is bounded to 500 MB per compiler/R/profile key, and caches compilation only. Tests always rerun. No global Makevars or compiler settings are edited. AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instrument the package; the test process preloads the matching Clang runtime. The host R binary is not instrumented, and leak detection is disabled for that host. --sanitizer-smoke proves detection with an intentionally invalid private fixture; its failure must be recognized before package checks can succeed.

Coverage uses a separate source copy because covr cleans and instruments its input. Install covr and xml2, then use the shared local/manual-CI runner:

Rscript tools/ci/run_coverage.R
Rscript tools/ci/run_coverage.R --filter '^(native-threads|compiled-fallback-parity)$' --require-native

The default runs the full installed suite and requires actual R and owned C++ coverage. A filter runs installed testthat files matching that expression; add --require-native when the selection promises native execution. Pure R selections may omit it. Reports, source and instrumented installation remain under a fresh archives/coverage/ directory. RDS, CSV, JSON and Cobertura XML include execution/source provenance. --html additionally requires DT and htmltools. --output-dir, --workspace, --install-path and --cobertura accept fresh destinations; existing outputs are rejected rather than replaced. Do not run a pkgload/devtools test helper inside coverage: it can replace the instrumented installed package. See the coverage test guidance.

Python analysis requires Ruff 0.17.2; the configuration selects correctness rules rather than enforcing a repository-wide formatting conversion:

python3 tools/ci/check_scripts.py
python3 tools/ci/check_scripts.py tools/dev/cpp_tooling.py

Install the pin with python3 -m pip install ruff==0.17.2 in the Python environment you use for maintenance. Formatting is opt-in: --format FILE.py changes only explicitly selected files. Both formatting modes reject directories. Lint defaults to maintained tools/ and tests/ Python files. Generated, vendor, private output and frozen replication sources stay excluded, including explicit selections. The runner never installs tools, auto-fixes lint or uses cached test results. Existing static CI runs this lint; native profiles remain explicit commands and coverage retains its manual workflow.

R and Stata parity

R is the numerical reference for shared methods. Compare identical inputs, row order, targets, fitted geometry, signals, weight controls and covariance definitions. Require exact discrete decisions and justified numeric tolerances; force and establish each engine, then test automatic fallback separately. High-level distance ties require exact represented selected-metric groups per target, rank-weight averaging over observations and actual-survivor deletion references. Bare supplied orders remain strict unless distances accompany them. Keep independent analytic/deletion references. Do not regenerate golden values merely to make a failure pass. The compiled-code policy owns the arithmetic contract.

The Stata checkout’s tests/R_TEST_CROSSWALK.md maps shared and R-only contracts. Its tools/generate_r_*.R scripts own cross-language fixtures, including reporting and saved-fit references. Run matching Stata regressions after an intentional shared-contract change. PLQR parity concerns supplied-coefficient moments; Stata has no density-backed coefficient inference.

With both checkouts present, verify mirrored native headers from the R root:

python3 ../RdistNN_stata/tools/ci/package_hygiene.py --r-root .

Reporting problems

Open a GitHub issue with a minimal example, expected/actual results and sessionInfo(). For numerical discrepancies, report whether they persist with options(RdistNN.use_compiled = FALSE). This selects R algorithms; source installation still requires compilation.

PRs should describe the final behavior, scope and verification. Maintainer documentation records current contracts and procedures; keep personal paths, session instructions, completed task lists, generated logs and execution receipts in private working records.

Checkout benchmarks

Install the development-only bench package and the current RdistNN, then run from the repository root:

Rscript tools/bench/run_bench.R l1 n=5000L reps=3L
Rscript tools/bench/run_bench.R l2 n=5000L reps=3L
Rscript tools/bench/run_bench.R cate n=1000L s=8L n_subsets=128L reps=3L
Rscript tools/bench/run_bench.R jackknife n=200L s=8L reps=3L

The same runner accepts the experimental plqr score benchmark. Shared scaffolding belongs under tools/bench/, outside installed code. Score runs compare current batch/scalar APIs and native reductions with explicit subset sums. Distance runs compare current public providers, R and native distances. Reporting benchmarks use tools/bench/bench_reporting.R; counters include a positive control before measurement. Timings are review evidence.
